title: Horse Sport Ireland staff protest at Minister Martin Heydon's office
seoTitle: Newbridge Horse Sport Ireland staff protest

tea.why: Staff protested over fears of liquidation and job losses if the Department of Agriculture fails to sign a key breeding services contract.
tea.want: Protesters demanded Minister Martin Heydon sign the National Breeding Services contract to secure the company's financial viability.
tea.changed: Nov 24: Horse Sport Ireland staff gathered outside Minister Martin Heydon's constituency office in Newbridge.

summary: Employees of Horse Sport Ireland demonstrated outside the Newbridge constituency office of Minister for Agriculture Martin Heydon on 24 November 2026. Organised by company staff, the demonstration called on the government to sign a contract for National Breeding Services to prevent the organisation from entering liquidation. Protesters warned that liquidation could jeopardize around 40 jobs and disrupt equine services, including issuing horse passports and processing Garda vetting for youth activities. A spokesperson for the minister stated that the Department of Agriculture is awaiting legal advice regarding EU public procurement and State aid rules, emphasizing the need for legally robust decisions during the examinership process.
demands: Execution of the National Breeding Services contract
Protection of jobs at Horse Sport Ireland
response: A spokesperson for Minister Martin Heydon stated that the department is awaiting urgent legal advice on EU public procurement and State aid rules to ensure any decision is legally robust.

updates.text: Horse Sport Ireland staff delivered a letter to Agriculture Minister Martin Heydon warning of job losses and service disruptions.
Staff demonstrated outside Minister Martin Heydon's office in Newbridge, urging the government to execute the breeding services contract.
